newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin considering Madrid trip during NATO summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin considering Madrid trip during NATO summit.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is considering going to Madrid during NATO's July summit at which the alliance is expected to invite some countries of eastern Europe to join, a deputy Russian foreign minister said.
Igor Ivanov told a news conference that Spanish King Juan Carlos, finishing a three-day visit to Moscow on Wednesday, said he would he happy to welcome Yeltsin in Madrid during the summit.
"President Yeltsin replied that the issue would be considered, taking into account all factors," Ivanov said.
Russia, fiercely opposed to NATO expansion, had said Yeltsin would not attend the summit, although Moscow has signaled its readiness to sign a charter on Russian-NATO relations in Paris on May 27.
The Western alliance is expected to use the Madrid summit to invite Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to join NATO.
Ivanov said talks on Russia's relationship with NATO would continue next week. "As you understand this topic is very delicate. Negotiations are very difficult," he said.

"As you know, yesterday there were expansive and detailed negotiations between Yevgeny Primakov, the Russian foreign minister, and Javier Solana, secretary-general of NATO, in Luxembourg. Next week these talks will be continued in Moscow."
Both sides have said they made "some progress" in the talks, but that further efforts were needed.
